oneliner.t: Opelika Democrat and U.S. Army veteran who says he spent about three decades in the Army and the defense intelligence community, unopposed for his party's nomination; first run for office, against Rep. Mike Rogers.

born.t: Birmingham, Alabama (date not found; per his Ballotpedia profile)

upbringing.t: McInnis grew up in Homewood and graduated from Homewood High School. In his Ballotpedia survey he says his father was a Korean War veteran who led a water-treatment plant and his mother was a long-time union member, and that he worked summers on a county road crew. He earned a bachelor's degree at Auburn (1983), served in the Army 1983–1989 as an Arabic linguist, and says he then spent a 28-year career in defense intelligence including postings in Qatar, Bahrain, Iraq and Afghanistan. After retiring and teaching at a college near Augusta, Ga., he returned to Auburn for a master's in history (2024) and now lives in Opelika. Family and service details are his own account, not independently corroborated.

education.deg: Master's (communications and international relations, per his survey)

career.role: Soldier, Arabic linguist (self-reported; says disabled veteran)
Intelligence officer (awards he lists: Joint Staff Civilian Commendation Medal; DIA Director's Intelligence Medal)
career.org: Defense intelligence community (reported as Defense Intelligence Agency)

career.role: Lead instructor at a college near Augusta, Ga.

platform.t: No one should lack basic coverage; opposes Republican health cuts, citing rural hospitals; says Medicaid cuts in the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' will worsen access in the rural district.
Says tariffs raise prices and hurt family farms; cites district poverty.
Make sure the ultra-rich and corporations pay their fair share.
Free quality education for all children; revive technical education and affordable college.
Reintroduce the DISCLOSE Act, require shareholder consent for corporate political spending, tax deductions for small donations; opposes term limits unless campaign-finance reform fails.
Criticizes detention and deportation without due process, efforts to end birthright citizenship and deploying troops in U.S. cities.

promises.t: Seek a seat on the House Intelligence or Armed Services Committee, then Veterans' Affairs or Agriculture.
Push to reintroduce the DISCLOSE Act and give tax deductions for small political donations.
Keep returning to the district to hear from constituents in person.
Run a nonviolent campaign rejecting threats and intimidation.

claims.claim: Served in the U.S. Army 1983–1989 as an Arabic linguist and is a disabled veteran.

record.t: Reported by local outlets as an Army veteran, but no service record was available to check dates or role.

claims.claim: Had a 28-year career in the defense intelligence community including Qatar, Bahrain, Iraq and Afghanistan, with a DIA Director's Intelligence Medal.

record.t: The Auburn Villager reports about 30 years in the Army and defense intelligence, including Iraq and Afghanistan, from a biography he provided; no agency record was available.

claims.claim: Earned a master's in history from Auburn in 2024.

record.t: Repeated by The Auburn Villager; no university record checked.

claims.claim: Rogers ran unopposed in 2024 — 'nobody in a democracy should ever run unopposed.'

record.t: Rogers won the 2024 general election with 97.93% of the vote; no other candidate is listed.

claims.claim: Rogers has represented the district since 2003.

record.t: Elected in 2002; in office since Jan. 3, 2003.

claims.claim: Voters in the district have lacked chances to connect with their representative for about a decade.
claims.short: No access to Rogers for decade

record.t: A Rogers in-person town hall in 2017 is documented, and his House site offers telephone town-hall sign-up; no 2025–2026 in-person town hall was found. The claim is broadly consistent with the record found but overstates it if telephone events count.
Census ACS district data were not retrieved in this pass.

claims.claim: Tariffs are raising prices and hurting farmers and family farms.

record.t: A general economic characterization; no specific figure given to check.

said.where: campaign announcement, Opelika Public Library (Auburn Villager, 2025-09-25)

record.t: The district's county list for the 119th Congress (2023 court-drawn map, unchanged for 2026) names 11 counties: Calhoun, Chambers, Cherokee, Clay, Cleburne, Etowah, Lee, Randolph, St. Clair, Tallapoosa and most of Talladega. The page's intro names only 10, so it is inconsistent; the Census district map it cites was not opened.

claims.claim: Medicaid budget cuts in the "One Big Beautiful Bill" will make rural health-care access worse.

said.where: campaign announcement, Opelika Public Library (Auburn Villager, 2025-09-25)

record.t: The checkable part holds: the 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21) cuts projected federal spending by over $1.2 trillion, mainly in Medicaid and SNAP. CBO estimates a $1.1 trillion net cut in direct spending over 2025–2034 and 10.9 million more uninsured. The law also creates a $50 billion rural health fund. Whether rural access gets worse overall is a forecast and is not rated.

claims.claim: The Trump administration is pushing to end birthright citizenship.

said.where: campaign announcement, Opelika Public Library (Auburn Villager, 2025-09-25)

record.t: Executive Order 14160 (Jan. 20, 2025) sought to deny citizenship at birth to children of unauthorized immigrants and of some temporary visitors. Courts blocked it, and on June 30, 2026 the Supreme Court held it unconstitutional in Trump v. Barbara (6–3). This was after his September 2025 remark.

claims.claim: The administration is deploying troops in U.S. cities.

said.where: campaign announcement, Opelika Public Library (Auburn Villager, 2025-09-25)

record.t: National Guard troops and Marines went to Los Angeles from June 2025, and about 2,000 Guard troops went to Washington, D.C. from August 2025. Deployments to other cities were announced later in 2025, and most were challenged in court.

checks.legal: CourtListener blocked (known limit); Justia/Alacourt and news-archive legal searches not run (search budget exhausted). Profiles reviewed (Ballotpedia, Auburn Villager, WTVM) mention no legal matters.
checks.foreign: No candidate financial disclosure located. FARA blocked (known limit). His self-described intelligence postings abroad were government service, not foreign ties.
checks.claims: Mechanical sample could not use the campaign site (leemcinnis4alabama.com unreachable). Used instead: his own Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (bio claims and the first issue statements) and his announcement and town-hall remarks as reported. No ads found. 7 checkable claims rated (2 true, 1 partly, 4 unverifiable) plus 1 opinion. Oct 8 pass: leemcinnis4alabama.com was still unreachable (proxy refused; no web.archive.org access). Reviewed the full announcement story (Auburn Villager) and the town-hall story (WTVM) and added 4 checkable claims from the announcement. Total: 12 claims, 7 rated true/partly (6 true, 1 partly), 4 unverifiable, 1 opinion. Not rated: his claim that the administration detains and deports immigrants "without due process" (needs court records not reached), and his remarks about Rogers' votes and oversight (characterizations).
checks.democracy: Reviewed his Ballotpedia survey, the Auburn Villager announcement story and the WTVM town-hall story. None contains a statement on the 2020 or 2024 results. His campaign site could not be reached, and new news searches could not be run (budget exhausted).

recordx.note: FEC committee page shows no RFAIs. Not an officeholder (no missed votes); candidate disclosure timeliness unknown.

research_notes: MONEY: FEC committee C00918433 (registered 2025-09-03), coverage 2025-07-01 to 2026-09-30 — the Q3 report is already in. All $60,787.05 came from individuals; no PAC, party or self money. The FEC page's figures don't reconcile: receipts minus disbursements is $31,887.22, but it shows ending cash of $9,461.79 — possibly totals and cash come from different reports; needs a human check of the filings. Ballotpedia's older figure ($10,160 raised) is superseded. Track AIPAC does not list him.
